relevance_reason: A large cohort study of epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS). It reports one patient with a de novo heterozygous GABRB1 variant, which adds GABRB1 as a new EIMFS gene and widens the DEE45 phenotype.

findings.statement: In a patient (Patient 63) with epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS), Burgess et al. (2019) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous variant in GABRB1 (chr4:47405633T>C, GRCh37), predicted to cause an ile247-to-thr (I247T) substitution. The variant was not found in the ExAC or gnomAD databases. SIFT predicted it to be deleterious, PolyPhen predicted it to be benign, and it was classified as likely pathogenic under ACMG criteria. The authors described GABRB1 as a new EIMFS gene that had previously been reported in other developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
quotes: 63 | GABRB1 | De Novo | Chr4:47405633T>C | p.I247T | NA | 0 | B | D | NA | WES | LP

We identified 2 individuals with pathogenic variants in GABA receptor subunit-encoding genes not previously associated with EIMFS, but reported in association with other developmental and epileptic encephalopathies: one case each for GABRA1 and GABRB1.
Three patients had heterozygous de novo variants in autosomal dominant genes: GABRA1, GABRB1, and ATP1A3.

phenotypes.text: epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures

findings.statement: Burgess et al. (2019) reported a patient with a de novo GABRB1 variant who was studied at age 2 years. The patient had focal seizures beginning at 4 months, with interhemispheric seizure migration (an inclusion criterion of the cohort). The patient also had profound to severe developmental impairment and hypotonia, and did not have epileptic spasms or microcephaly.
quotes: All patients had evidence of interhemispheric seizure migration, either clinically and/or by EEG, in accordance with our inclusion criteria.

findings.statement: Burgess et al. (2019) found causative variants in 93 of 135 patients with EIMFS (69%), spread across 23 genes. Nine of these genes were new to EIMFS, among them GABRA1 and GABRB1. The authors emphasized the role of GABA-related mechanisms and noted that 3 patients carried variants in the known EIMFS gene GABRB3.
quotes: Ninety-three of 135 (69%) had causative variants (42/55 previously reported) across 23 genes, including 9 novel EIMFS genes: de novo dominant GABRA1, GABRB1, ATP1A3; X-linked CDKL5, PIGA; and recessive ITPA, AIMP1, KARS, WWOX.

We emphasize the role of GABA-related mechanisms by implicating two new GABA receptor subunit genes, GABRA1 and GABRB1, along with our finding that three patients had variants in the known EIMFS gene GABRB3.

relevance_reason: Reports a patient with epileptic encephalopathy carrying a de novo GABRB1 mutation, the gene underlying DEE45. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Lien et al. (2016) reported a second patient with epileptic encephalopathy who carried a de novo mutation in the GABRB1 gene.
quotes: A second patient with a De Novo GABRB1 mutation and epileptic encephalopathy.

relevance_reason: Functional characterization in HEK293T cells of the de novo GABRB1 F246S variant found in a patient with infantile spasms (identified by Epi4K). The paper also studies GABRB3 variants, which are relevant to a different entry.

findings.statement: Janve et al. (2016) studied a de novo heterozygous F246S mutation in the GABRB1 gene, which the Epi4K Consortium had found in a child with infantile spasms. F246 is a residue that is the same in all GABA-A receptor subunits and lies in transmembrane domain 1. When expressed with alpha-1 and gamma-2L subunits in HEK293T cells, the mutation reduced GABA-evoked peak current density by 25% in the homozygous condition and had no effect in the heterozygous condition. It slowed current deactivation. The authors concluded that the mutation impaired GABA-A receptor function and suggested that GABRB1 is a candidate human epilepsy gene.
quotes: Additionally one IS patient had a mutation in the GABAA receptor β1 subunit gene (GABRB1(F246S)).
Under similar hom expression conditions, current densities from cells expressing β1(F246S) subunits had a minor (25%) reduction of peak current densities
Despite lack of association with epilepsy syndromes, our results suggest GABRB1 as a candidate human epilepsy gene.

findings.statement: In single-channel recordings, Janve et al. (2016) found that receptors with the GABRB1 F246S mutation had normal open probability despite a lower opening frequency. The mutation produced a gain of function, with about 3.75-fold longer mean open time and about 3.2-fold longer burst duration. It also lowered single-channel conductance to about 21 pS. The authors proposed that faster rise time and slower deactivation would lengthen inhibitory postsynaptic currents but would reduce charge transfer during later currents, resulting in a net loss of GABAergic inhibition.
quotes: for the β1(F246S) subunit mutation, a gain of function resulted in increased mean open time (~3.75 fold) and burst duration (~3.2 fold) from prolonged openings.
In contrast, the β1(F246S) subunit mutation reduced the deactivation rate (increased weighted deactivation rate constant) compared to wt currents
Counter intuitively, both faster and slower deactivation would result in the net loss of GABAergic inhibition

findings.statement: Janve et al. (2016) found that the GABRB1 F246S mutation raised whole-cell holding currents about 5-fold in the homozygous condition, and these currents were partly blocked by zinc. In the absence of GABA, it increased spontaneous single-channel open probability 4-fold. Surface levels of the mutant beta-1 subunit were slightly but significantly lower, while total levels were unchanged. The authors suggested that receptors containing the mutant subunit opened spontaneously. Structural modeling predicted rearrangements in the coupling zone that spread to the transmembrane domains.
quotes: Both LGS-associated GABRB3(E180G) and IS-associated GABRB1(F246S) mutations significantly increased (~5 fold) holding currents recorded from α1βγ2L receptors, suggesting spontaneous channel openings in hom, but not het, conditions
GABAA receptors containing the β1(F246S) subunit mutation increased spontaneous Po by 4-fold (Figure 8F, right panel) but did not alter single-channel conductance.
Reduced surface β1(F246S) levels without a reduction in the total levels suggest that mutant subunits affected the assembly and/or trafficking of GABAA heteromeric or β1 homomeric receptors

relevance_reason: The exome screen of 264 epileptic encephalopathy trios found a de novo GABRB1 mutation in one patient. That is the gene for DEE45. The supplied text does not give the variant, the patient's phenotype or any functional data.

findings.statement: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) sequenced the exomes of 264 probands with infantile spasms or Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and their parents. They identified a de novo mutation in the GABRB1 gene in one patient. The supplied text does not specify the variant or the patient's phenotype. This was one of six de novo mutations affecting subunits of the GABA-A receptor; the other five were four in GABRB3 and one in GABRA1. The authors suggested that rare mutations in different genes may converge on shared pathways.
quotes: In support of a hypothesis that individual rare mutations in different genes may converge on pathways, we draw attention to the six mutations that all affect subunits of the gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) ionotropic receptor (four in GABRB3, and one each in GABRA1 and GABRB1)
We sequenced the exomes of 264 probands, and their parents, and confirmed 329 de novo mutations.

findings.statement: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) studied patients from the Epilepsy Phenome/Genome Project with infantile spasms (n = 149) or Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (n = 115). Patients with infantile spasms were required to have hypsarrhythmia on EEG. Patients with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome were required to have a slow or disorganized EEG background with generalized spike-and-wave activity or generalized paroxysmal fast activity. All patients had brain MRI or CT read as normal, mild diffuse atrophy or focal cortical dysplasia. None had moderate-to-severe developmental impairment before seizure onset.
quotes: Here we report a screen for de novo mutations in patients with two classical epileptic encephalopathies: infantile spasms (n = 149) and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (n = 115).
IS patients were required to have hypsarrhythmia or a hypsarrhythmia on EEG.
All IS and LGS patients had an MRI or CT scan interpreted as normal, mild diffuse atrophy or focal cortical dysplasia.
